audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge (W) blocks ATTACKS that would hit Shen or his allies near the spirit blade. Both layers treat it as a general damage wall — full dontsFull[1].t reads 'Fight his W block' and content wants.foe[0] 'Farm safely with spirit blade and shield-tank your W' — and neither says what it actually stops.
audit.why: It is the difference between standing there doing nothing and continuing to win the trade. Zac's damage inside Shen's W is split: his basic attacks are stopped, but Unstable Matter is an ability on a flat 5s cooldown and keeps burning. Told only 'fight his W block', the player backs out of a zone he could still be dealing %max-health damage inside. This is the most-used ability in the matchup at 16s rank 1, so the correction applies several times a minute.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge stops attacks. Keep casting Unstable Matter (W) inside it rather than trying to auto through — your abilities still land while your basics are eaten.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (Spirit's Refuge: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked', cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10)

audit.whatIsWrong: Shen's energy costs are absent from both layers. Shadow Dash costs 150 energy of a 200 pool; Twilight Assault costs 140 at rank 1; Spirit's Refuge costs 40. Shadow Dash is also on 18s at rank 1.
audit.why: This is the whole punish window in a matchup Zac loses at 46.32%, and neither layer mentions it. A Shen who has just taunted has spent 150 of 200 energy — he cannot pay 140 for Twilight Assault, so for the following seconds the taunt is gone AND his max-health damage is gone AND he is on an 18s cooldown at rank 1. That is the single largest opening Zac gets in this lane, and the entry currently only tells the player to 'dodge his E taunt'. Dodging it and immediately walking away wastes the exact window worth having.
audit.corrected: Shadow Dash: 18s at rank 1, 150 of his 200 energy. Once he spends it he cannot afford Twilight Assault (140 at rank 1) either. Do not just dodge the taunt — commit into the seconds after it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (Shadow Dash cost 150, cooldown 18/16/14/12/10; Twilight Assault cost 140/130/120/110/100; energy pool 200 is standard for energy champions)

audit.whatIsWrong: Twilight Assault (Q) deals damage based on the target's maximum health. The full layer prescribes Heartsteel as Zac's core item ('HP feeds everything') and neither layer connects the two.
audit.why: In a lane Zac already loses, the recommended item is scaling the enemy's primary damage ability. Twilight Assault is 8s at rank 1 and is Shen's most frequent damage source, so more max health means more damage taken on every single cast. The build is not wrong outright — Zac needs the health — but the entry should say that resistances matter more here than in a generic tank lane, and it currently says the opposite.
audit.corrected: Twilight Assault scales on your maximum health. Weight armour and MR earlier than usual alongside the health, because health is the stat that feeds his 8s ability.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (Twilight Assault: 'dealing damage based on the target's max health', cooldown 8/7.25/6.5/5.75/5)

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[2].text reads 'With Sunfire and boots your Q-Q gap-close and W AoE start out-trading his sword swings'. Zac has no Q gap-close — Stretching Strikes is an 800-range grab and the gap-close is Elastic Slingshot (E).
audit.why: It names the wrong ability for the player's own core action at the exact stage the entry says the lane starts turning. A player following it literally would try to close distance with Q, which pulls the enemy toward him rather than moving him, and would leave E unspent.
audit.corrected: Your gap-close is Elastic Slingshot (E). Stretching Strikes (Q) is an 800-range grab, not a movement tool.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (E: Elastic Slingshot, dash flag; Q: Stretching Strikes, range 800, no dash flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4].why is the shared boilerplate line. content whys[4] says 'At 6 Stand United gives Shen map pressure Zac can't match', with no number.
audit.why: Stand United is 200s at rank 1 — one of the longest cooldowns in the game — and it is a channel followed by a teleport away. Framed only as pressure Zac 'can't match', it reads as a permanent disadvantage. Framed with the number, it reads as what it is: twice every lane phase Shen physically leaves, and each departure is a free shove and plate for Zac if he is watching for it.
audit.corrected: Stand United: 200/180/160s, global, channelled. Each cast takes him out of lane — that is the tempo window, not a thing to fear.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (Stand United: cooldown 200/180/160, global + channel flags)

notes: This is the weakest matchup in my slice (46.32% over 190 games) and it had the most missing. THE WINDOW: Shadow Dash costs 150 of Shen's 200 energy and sits on 18s at rank 1; once he taunts he cannot pay the 140 energy for Twilight Assault either. That compound window — no taunt, no max-health damage, 18s to wait — is the largest opening Zac gets in this lane and neither layer mentioned energy at all. The existing advice stopped at 'dodge his E taunt', which throws the window away. SECOND: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks; Unstable Matter is an ability on a flat 5s cooldown and keeps working inside it, so the correct play in his W is to keep casting rather than to disengage. Both layers described it only as a wall to avoid. THIRD: Twilight Assault scales on the target's maximum health while the full layer prescribes Heartsteel as core — same conflict as the Sett entry, and it matters more here because Zac is already behind. FOURTH: fixed 'your Q-Q gap-close' in spikes[2].text — Zac's gap-close is E; Q is an 800-range grab. The suspectNames hit on spikes[3].text ('Let's Bounce') is a FALSE POSITIVE: the file already reads 'Let's Bounce! (R)' with the exclamation mark, matching the kit exactly.
